clue.text: Drum almost filled with a fruit

indicators.note: the shortened drum name has the next letter put inside it, as a container is filled
almost the whole drum name, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a tom-tom is a tall drum played with the hands
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drum stuffed with a piece of fruit, presumably by a prankster in the band.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically the tomato is a fruit, a seed-bearing body grown from a flower, though cooks treat it as a vegetable.

clue.text: Dull sound when round gong that's fingered

indicators.note: the dull-sound word goes round the honour, enclosing it

parts.note: a thud is a heavy muffled noise
slang for a medal or honour, here the MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A muffled noise sounds when someone handles a gong.
explanation.walkthrough: A gong in British slang is a medal or honour; the MBE is a common one awarded by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To thumb something is to touch or leaf through it with the fingers, so a thumbed book has been handled.

clue.text: Get out having escaped pea: try fruit

indicators.note: the named letters have left the pea's name, so they are taken out of it

parts.note: a mangetout is a pea eaten pod and all
these words name the letters to be removed, read literally
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: An order to leave, then a pea has run off, then an encouragement to try some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get out' reads as a command but is the literal string removed from MANGETOUT, a flat pea pod eaten whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The mango is a tropical stone fruit with sweet orange flesh.

clue.text: Carving on reservation, painted plate needing time for inscription

indicators.note: the time word is written into the plate word, as an inscription is cut into a surface

parts.note: tole is lacquered or painted tinplate, used for decorative trays
tempo is the time or speed of a piece of music

explanation.surface: A carved object on a reservation alongside a painted plate that needs a date inscribed.
explanation.walkthrough: TOLE is an uncommon word: decorative painted metalware, often trays.
explanation.definitionFit: Totem poles are tall carved wooden posts made by Native peoples of the Pacific Northwest, so they stand on reservations.

clue.text: See 8
Actor putting the flora in Florida?

parts.note: Orlando is a city in Florida, home of the theme parks
flora is plant life, and a bloom is a flower

explanation.surface: A whimsical question: what would an actor be called if you put the flowers in Florida?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also reads as a riddle: a flower placed in a Florida city.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando Bloom is the English film star who played Legolas in The Lord of the Rings.

clue.text: …s game

parts.note: the dots stand in for this clue's own number, five
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clue made almost entirely of dots and a game, inviting the solver to fill in the blank.
explanation.walkthrough: This is clue 5, so the dots before the s are read as its number, FIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fives is a British handball-style court sport in which the ball is struck with a gloved hand.

clue.text: Part sung in key, another key briefly eclipsing it

indicators.note: the shortened key name covers the first key, holding it inside
the second key's name is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: Control is another computer keyboard key
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A musical part sung in one key while another key casts a shadow over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' tempts a musical reading, but both keys are on a computer keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The contralto is the lowest female voice part in a choir or opera.

clue.text: Take stock when philosopher overheard?

indicators.note: heard rather than read, so the philosopher's name gives a word that sounds like it

parts.note: Bertrand Russell, the British philosopher

explanation.surface: Taking stock of a situation while a philosopher is listening in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take stock' sounds like an audit, but stock here is livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: To rustle is to steal cattle or horses, literally taking livestock.

clue.text: Inside job?

definitions.meaning: slang for being in jail, as in doing time inside
the employment of someone who works in that place

explanation.walkthrough: An inside job is usually a crime committed with help from within; here it is simply work done inside a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A warder who guards inmates has a job literally within the walls of a jail.

clue.text: Odd tuna swimming round northern river in Russia

indicators.note: the rearranged fish letters go round the abbreviation for northern
a fish swimming moves about, so the letters of tuna are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the fish's own letters
the Ural flows from the Ural Mountains to the Caspian Sea

explanation.surface: A strange sight: a tuna swimming around a northern Russian river.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unnatural is abnormal or strange, departing from what is expected.

clue.text: Beauty pageants uneventful, though some tripping over

indicators.note: falling head over heels, so the run of letters is turned backwards
only some of the letters of these words are taken, the run spanning them

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the end of pageants and the start of uneventful

explanation.surface: Beauty pageants are dull affairs, though some contestants do fall over.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus was the Roman goddess of love, and her name stands for any great beauty.

clue.text: See 4 down
Left-leaning Stalinist not quite right after revolution

indicators.note: once overturned, the letters are rearranged into a new order
the word falls short of complete, so its last letter goes

parts.note: taken as written before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A left-wing Stalinist who is not quite right-wing once the revolution has happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left-leaning' and 'revolution' suggest politics, but the answer means left-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinistral means on or favouring the left side, from the Latin for left.

clue.text: Shrink once had nurses excited at the outset

indicators.note: holds as a nurse cradles a baby, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: did own is the past tense of possess

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is used

parts.note: its first letter, at the outset of the word

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist who once had nurses getting excited at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrink' reads as a psychiatrist, but it is the verb meaning to lessen.
explanation.definitionFit: To die down is to subside or lessen in strength, as a fire or a noise does.

clue.text: Looking surprised — as a snail?

definitions.meaning: first sense: an idiom for being astonished, eyes bulging
second sense: a snail's eyes really are carried on ...

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for astonishment is literally true of a snail, whose eyes sit at the tips of its tentacles.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a British idiom for staring in amazement, and literally describes the eyes of a garden snail.

clue.text: Blue essentially follows decoration of room in gold

indicators.note: decorating rearranges a room, so its letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: only the essence, the inner letters, of the word is kept

parts.note: the inner letters of the word, without its first and last

explanation.surface: Blue paint follows a gold decorating scheme for a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Ormolu is gilded bronze or a gold-coloured alloy used on furniture mounts.

clue.text: Brilliant at music, strange being on tour of Australia

indicators.note: the alien goes around the country, so it encloses the abbreviation

parts.note: a Martian is an alien from Mars
Oz is the informal name for Australia

explanation.surface: A gifted musician and an alien on tour around Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozartian describes something with the genius and elegance associated with Mozart's compositions.

clue.text: Echoing note resounding initially — with this?

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: its first letter, taken initially

indicators.note: an echo comes back, so the note's name is turned backwards

parts.note: a breve is a long musical note

explanation.surface: A note echoing and resounding at first, produced by some sound effect.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the question at the end: the whole clue describes the effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverb is a sound-engineering effect adding reverberation, making a note seem to echo.

clue.text: Platform where meaty sandwiches left

indicators.note: puts between two layers, so the meaty word encloses the other piece

parts.note: bacony means like bacon, a playful coinage

explanation.surface: A platform where meat sandwiches are left lying around.
explanation.definitionFit: A balcony is a raised platform projecting from a building or overlooking a theatre.

clue.text: Ultimately, buttock and lower back prodded by a couple of unknowns — one's an idiot

indicators.note: the other letters poke into it, so they go inside
the word is read from back to front

parts.note: to lower is to look threatening, the same as cow in the sense of intimidate
taken as written
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns; two of them here are z

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the last letter of the word, ultimately

explanation.surface: A cheeky scene of someone's backside and lower back being poked, ending with an insult.
explanation.walkthrough: Wazzock is northern English slang for a fool; lower (rhymes with flower) means to scowl, like cow meaning to cow someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Wazzock is British slang for a stupid or annoying person, a fool.

clue.text: Bottomless den concealed by foxy to a great extent

indicators.note: hidden inside the other word, so the shortened den goes within it

parts.note: a fox is proverbially sly, so foxy means wily

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom is the last letter, which is removed

parts.note: taken as written before its bottom letter goes

explanation.surface: A fox's den, impossibly deep, kept hidden by the cunning animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Widely means over a broad range or to a large degree, as in widely admired.

clue.text: Youth and king upset about fascist force in parliament

indicators.note: the reversed letters go around the fascist force
knocked over, so in a down clue the letters are reversed

parts.note: a teen is a young person
the SS was the Nazi paramilitary force

explanation.surface: A young person and a monarch upset about fascist forces in their parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Knesset is the parliament of Israel, sitting in Jerusalem.

clue.text: See 14
River having dried up on the banks, used a digger

indicators.note: the drying word lies either side of the river, like its two banks

parts.note: towelled means rubbed dry with a towel

explanation.surface: A river that dried up between its banks, where someone then dug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digger' suggests a mechanical excavator, but it is a small hand tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A trowel is a small gardening tool for digging, so trowelled means dug with one.

clue.text: Miss little monster having sliced off head

indicators.note: the first letter, the head of the word, is cut off

parts.note: a terror is a badly behaved child

explanation.surface: A young lady who has beheaded a tiny monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a girl's title, but it is the noun meaning a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A miss is a failure or mistake, so it serves as a synonym for an error.

clue.text: Grand nicked by one scoundrel — or another?

indicators.note: stolen by, taken into the possession of, so the grand goes inside

parts.note: a roué is a debauched man, a rake

explanation.surface: A thousand pounds pinched by a rascal, or perhaps a different rascal.
explanation.walkthrough: Grand is slang for a thousand, abbreviated G.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest rascal, another kind of villain alongside the rake.

clue.text: Type of fruit, one in apple

indicators.note: the numeral one goes inside the apple's name

parts.note: Gala is a popular apple variety

explanation.surface: A kind of fruit, with one inside an apple.
explanation.definitionFit: Galia is a variety of melon with green flesh and a netted rind.

clue.text: Future time in firm reviewed

indicators.note: looked at again, back to front, so the letters are reversed
the time abbreviation goes inside the other word

parts.note: real in the sense of solid, actual

explanation.surface: A future date at which the company will be inspected.
explanation.definitionFit: Later as an adjective means coming afterwards, belonging to a time still ahead.

clue.text: Fidelio's Léonore, originally in disguise here: well, well, well!

definitions.note: many wells, as in an oilfield

indicators.note: disguised, the letters are rearranged into a new form

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: only the first letter of the name is used

parts.note: the first letter of the heroine's name

explanation.surface: In Beethoven's opera Fidelio, the heroine Leonore disguises herself as the man Fidelio.
explanation.walkthrough: The opera reference is apt: Leonore really is in disguise as Fidelio. The exclamation of surprise doubles as a description of a place full of wells.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil fields are areas dotted with many drilled wells extracting petroleum.

clue.text: Collaboration with offender and my Lord on the radio?

indicators.note: on the radio means the words are heard spoken, so their sound gives the answer

parts.note: a sinner is an offender, and gee is a mild exclamation, a minced form of Jesus, like 'my Lord!'

explanation.surface: A broadcast teaming up a criminal with a peer of the realm.
explanation.walkthrough: SINNER GEE said aloud gives SYNERGY. 'my Lord' looks like a peer, but it is an exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Synergy is the combined effect of parties working together, greater than their separate efforts.

clue.text: Whole testament, account in it

indicators.note: these pieces are placed inside the other word

parts.note: taken as written
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: The whole testament, with an account included.
explanation.definitionFit: Intact means undamaged and complete, with nothing missing.
